desc: Parse input: N, M, X and edge list; build both forward adjacency `g0` and reversed adjacency `g1`.
Implement Dijkstra over states encoded as `v * 2 + p` (or `p * N + v`), with a distance array of size 2N initialized to infinity.
Add transitions: relax neighbors via `g0[v]`/`g1[v]` with cost 1, and relax the same vertex with flipped parity with cost X.
Start from state (1, 0); after Dijkstra, answer is `min(dist[N][0], dist[N][1])`.
Use 64-bit integers (Python ints are fine) and fast I/O (`sys.stdin.buffer`) to handle N, M up to 2e5.
Verify logic mentally against samples: sample 1 gives 4, sample 2 gives 3, sample 3 gives large value requiring 64-bit.
Write the complete Python program with solve(), fast parsing via sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(), heapq-based Dijkstra, and print the answer; enclose in required delimiters.
